source: Supplied cvs_twin_template YAML, 16 October 2026. Stored as data so the agent reads the template rather than hard-coding it.

customerFirst: Start with the customer, not the solution.
Use customer value creation as the organising spine.
Translate business strategy into value-stream friction, measurable outcomes and validation actions.
evidenceDiscipline: Separate validated evidence, public signals, user-provided signals, industry patterns, assumptions and hypotheses.
Label every insight with source type, confidence and validation status.
valueSelling: Map every opportunity to outcomes, KPIs, value-stream stages, stakeholders and validation evidence.
Frame technology as capability enablement, not the starting point.
Prioritise measurable value, risk reduction, adoption and operating model readiness.
partnerEcosystem: Label partner roles as evidenced, inferred, assumed or to-be-validated.
Show joint pursuit implications and P360 mapping guidance.
responsibleAi: Include Responsible AI, governance, provenance, human review and data sensitivity.
Flag sensitive, confidential or restricted signals.
Include RAI risk, auditability and human-in-the-loop requirements for AI use cases.

cvsFlow.name: Understand
cvsFlow.description: Know the customer, industry, organisation, market, strategy, metrics and ecosystem.
cvsFlow.shows: Customer context, strategy signals, stakeholder landscape and evidence base.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: Where value may be created, delayed, protected or improved.

cvsFlow.name: Value Twin
cvsFlow.description: Map the customer value stream into visual nodes, signals, metrics and feedback loops.
cvsFlow.shows: How value flows across the business from trigger to outcome.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: Where friction, delay, risk, waste or missed opportunity may exist.

cvsFlow.name: Current State
cvsFlow.description: Establish operating, technical and organisational reality.
cvsFlow.shows: As-is maturity, known gaps, assumptions and validation questions.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: What must be understood before proposing technology or change.

cvsFlow.name: Outcomes
cvsFlow.description: Connect friction to measurable outcomes and KPIs.
cvsFlow.shows: Outcome themes, KPI relationships and stakeholder relevance.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: Which value hypotheses are worth validating.

cvsFlow.name: Capabilities
cvsFlow.description: Map gaps to required capabilities and portfolio domains.
cvsFlow.shows: Capabilities required to improve the value stream.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: Where portfolio alignment may help, without becoming product-led.

cvsFlow.name: Partners
cvsFlow.description: Map partner roles, influence, delivery fit and co-sell motion.
cvsFlow.shows: Evidenced and inferred partner roles across advisory, integration, managed services and adoption.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: Who can help create, deliver, scale or validate the outcome.

cvsFlow.name: Validate
cvsFlow.description: Validate through evidence, pilots, governance, adoption and measurement.
cvsFlow.shows: Validation gates, use case readiness, RAI risk and next actions.
cvsFlow.tellsUs: What should move forward, pause, be redesigned or be rejected.
cvsFlow.output: Validated roadmap and AI value twin

sellingComparison.solutionLed: Product, feature, architecture or vendor agenda.
sellingComparison.outcomeAligned: Customer strategy, value-stream friction and measurable outcomes.

sellingComparison.solutionLed: Qualifies fit for a known solution.
sellingComparison.outcomeAligned: Explores how value is created, delayed, lost or exposed to risk.
Maps executive, operating, technical, finance, partner and CX stakeholders.
Defines value hypotheses first and validates them with evidence.

sellingComparison.solutionLed: Partner is attached after solution shaping.
sellingComparison.outcomeAligned: Partner role is mapped to value creation, validation, delivery and adoption.

sellingComparison.solutionLed: AI ideas are positioned as innovation or automation.
sellingComparison.outcomeAligned: AI use cases are tied to value-stream friction, KPIs, risk and validation gates.

knowledgeGraphLayers.label: Industry context
knowledgeGraphLayers.description: What the industry is and what pressures act on it.

knowledgeGraphLayers.label: Industry value streams
knowledgeGraphLayers.description: The value streams the industry runs in general.

knowledgeGraphLayers.label: Customer value streams
knowledgeGraphLayers.description: How this customer appears to run those streams, inferred from their reporting.

knowledgeGraphLayers.label: Organisation and functions
knowledgeGraphLayers.description: The functions that own each customer value stream.

knowledgeGraphLayers.label: Personas
knowledgeGraphLayers.description: The roles inside each function that decide, measure and approve.

interactions: Knowledge graph node click updates the detail panel
Layer filter narrows the graph to one concept level
Evidence filter narrows the graph by evidence class
technicalConstraints: All dashboard content renders from the generated pack
No external research calls at runtime

generationRules: Generate the JSON pack first, then render it.
Mark all unvalidated items clearly as hypotheses.
Do not invent evidence. Where evidence is absent, create a validation question.
Use industry patterns only as hypotheses unless supported by evidence.
Prioritise capability needs before portfolio mapping.
Ensure every AI use case has RAI risk, data dependency and validation action.
